nvmstudio.autoLoadArxml.description: Automatically load an ARXML file from the same directory as the opened binary (if present).

nvmstudio.nvm.allowExternalEngines.description: Master switch for NVM layout engines. When a layout descriptor (`*.nvmlayout.json`) declares an `engineScript`/`engine`, it is executed to parse the dump — but only in the desktop extension host, in a trusted workspace, and after a one-time per-file confirmation. Set to `false` to disable engines entirely for locked-down environments.

enumDescriptions: NVM workbench: Blocks table, Hex, Inspector, Overview, Tree and Annotations as freely arrangeable panels inside the editor, with built-in layout presets.
Classic: the hex editor only (structure views stay in the NVM Studio sidebar).
nvmstudio.nvm.layoutMode.description: How an NVM dump is presented in the editor. Reopen the dump after changing this setting.

enumDescriptions: Store bookmarks/tags/notes in a portable sidecar file next to the dump (<dump>.nvmstudio.json + a <dump>.nvmstudio/ folder for note markdown/images).
Store annotations in VS Code workspace state (not shareable, no files created).
nvmstudio.nvm.annotationStorage.description: Where NVM bookmarks, tags and notes are persisted.

nvmstudio.nvm.workspaceRoots.markdownDescription: Root folders searched **recursively** to auto-find dependency files a layout descriptor declares (e.g. `Fee_Lcfg.c`, `Dem_Lcfg.h`, `*.arxml`) when they aren't next to the dump or in `./conf`/`../conf`. This is **not** the dump folder and **not** the auto-discovery `./conf`/`../conf` (those are always searched). Supports `${workspaceFolder}` and `${workspaceFolder:Name}`. When several files share a name you'll be asked which to use, and the choice is remembered (see `#nvmstudio.nvm.fileChoices#`). The plugin never downloads files — fetch remote ones into a root yourself.

nvmstudio.nvm.layoutRoots.markdownDescription: Global folders scanned for layout **descriptors** (`*.nvmlayout.json`) so they don't have to sit next to each dump. Each listed folder **and its `conf/` subfolder** are scanned directly (works for absolute paths outside the workspace, e.g. a shared user folder). This is separate from `#nvmstudio.nvm.workspaceRoots#`, which finds the descriptor's declared **source** files. Supports `${workspaceFolder}` and `${workspaceFolder:Name}`.

nvmstudio.nvm.fileChoices.markdownDescription: Remembered dependency-file disambiguation choices (base file name → `{ relPath, root }`), written automatically when you pick among duplicates. Portable/shareable: paths are relative to a workspace root so they re-resolve on another machine. Use the command **NVM: Reselect Dependency File** to change a choice. A machine-local absolute-path cache is kept separately in workspace state.

enumDescriptions: The AI decides which skills to use (lexical pre-filter + model choice); `skill:<name>` forces one.
Only skills named explicitly with `skill:<name>` are used.
Skills are disabled everywhere (AI, decoding, field docs).
nvmstudio.nvm.skills.mode.markdownDescription: How NVM Studio skills (playbooks + block knowledge, see `docs/features/skills.md`) are used.

nvmstudio.nvm.skillRoots.markdownDescription: Extra folders scanned for skills (each folder **and its `skills/` subfolder**; every subfolder with a `SKILL.md` is one skill). Highest priority. Supports `${workspaceFolder}`. Other roots: `skills/` beside layout descriptors, `<workspace>/.nvmstudio/skills`, `~/nvmstudio/skills` (or `$NVMSTUDIO_HOME/skills`), and the built-in skills. Workspace roots are only used in a trusted workspace.

nvmstudio.nvm.skills.catalogSize.markdownDescription: Maximum number of skills advertised to the AI per request (Top-K of the lexical pre-filter).

nvmstudio.nvm.skills.applyStructs.markdownDescription: Let block skills' `struct` catalogs decode bound blocks (and be offered to engines as a `structCatalog` overlay).

nvmstudio.nvm.chat.maxToolRounds.markdownDescription: Maximum tool-calling rounds per `@nvm` request. Deep investigations that combine several skills may need more.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_loadStatus
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Explain whether and how the active dump was recognized: descriptors found, declared source files (resolved / missing, required / optional), pinned layout profile, provider and block count — plus concrete next steps when nothing was parsed. Use it when the user asks why the dump is shown as plain hex, why blocks are missing, or what configuration is in effect.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_reveal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show a block (by name or id) or a byte offset to the user: scrolls the hex view, selects and highlights the owning block, and syncs the Blocks table / Inspector. Use it whenever you point the user at a block or address so they can verify your evidence. View-only.

block.description: Block name or id (exact, or a unique substring).

offset.description: Editor byte offset (number or hex string like 0x3A0828). Used when no block is given.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_showView
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Open (or focus) a view in the user's NVM workbench. Views: nvm.blocksTable (block table), nvm.hex (raw bytes), nvm.inspector (decoded value tree), nvm.overview (dump summary), nvm.blocksTree (blocks by sector / write order / identity), nvm.annotations (bookmarks, notes, tags), nvm.customView (the user's comparison views). View-only.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_filterTable
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Set the Blocks table's search text, sort column, visible columns and 'latest only' flag (replaces the current filter; call with no arguments to clear it). Column keys are the block attribute keys (see nvm_describeDump) plus __name, __offset, __length. Use it to show the user the blocks your answer is about. View-only.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against all visible cells (e.g. a block name family like 'Dem').

columns.description: Column keys to show, in order (the name column is always shown).

latestOnly.description: Only show the newest instance of each logical block.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_applyLayout
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Arrange the user's NVM workbench. Either pick a built-in preset (builtin.tableFocus, builtin.hexFocus, builtin.structure, builtin.investigate, builtin.overview) or pass a layout tree: { root: node } where node = { split: 'horizontal'|'vertical', sizes?: number[], children: node[] } or { tabs: [{ view: '<view id>', params?: {...} }] }. 'horizontal' places children side by side. The user can always restore the preset with Reset. View-only.

layout.description: Ad-hoc layout: { root: node } (see tool description).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_listBlocks
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the parsed NVM blocks of the active hex-editor dump (name, offset, length, field count). Paged: pass limit/offset; the result states whether more blocks exist.

limit.description: Max blocks to return (default 100, hard cap 500).

offset.description: Index of the first block to return, for paging (default 0).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_describeDump
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return an EXACT whole-dump aggregate for the active hex-editor dump, computed on the host over ALL blocks (never truncated). Includes total block count, decoded-block count, distinct decoded-structure count, block counts grouped by numeric name family (e.g. DemPrimaryDataBlock*), counts grouped by decoded-structure fingerprint, and value distributions of vendor-neutral attributes. Use this FIRST to answer 'how many X blocks' questions instead of counting a paged list.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_searchBlocks
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the active dump's blocks by a case-insensitive substring of the block name/id, an attribute label/value, a decoded field name, or by a byte offset (0x.. or decimal) that falls inside a block. Paged. Prefer this over listing all blocks on large dumps.

query.description: Substring of a block name/id, or a byte offset (0x.. or decimal).

limit.description: Max blocks to return (default 100, hard cap 500).

offset.description: Index of the first match to return, for paging (default 0).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_getDecoded
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return a single block's business-decoded field tree (values, units, enum labels), depth- and node-capped so large structures don't overflow. Use instead of analyzeBlock when you need decoded values rather than raw geometry.

name.description: The block name (or a substring) whose decoded tree to return.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_readBytes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a bounded window of raw bytes (hard cap 4096 bytes) from the active dump at a byte offset and return them as space-separated hex. Use for inspecting actual bytes without loading the whole file.

length.description: Number of bytes to read (hard cap 4096).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_createNote
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create ONE anchored note on the active dump. Use sparingly — only for a specific finding, never a whole-file summary. The note MUST target a block (blockName) or a byte range (start/end) and MUST have a meaningful title and body. The user is asked to confirm before the note is written.

blockName.description: Anchor the note to this block's byte range (preferred). Omit if using start/end.

start.description: Start byte offset to anchor to (used when blockName is omitted).

end.description: Exclusive end byte offset of the range (optional; defaults to start+1).

body.description: The note's Markdown body — the actual finding (required).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_analyzeBlock
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return the fields and metadata of a single NVM block in the active dump, matched by name.

name.description: The block name (or a substring) to analyze.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_listAnnotations
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the bookmarks, tags and notes the user created on the active NVM dump.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_exportReport
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Produce a Markdown analysis report for the active NVM dump combining parsed blocks with the user's bookmarks, tags and notes.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_riskDetection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Run heuristic checks over the active NVM dump's parsed blocks (unresolved names, zero-length blocks, overlaps) and report potential risks.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_listSkills
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List NVM Studio skills: 'playbook' skills describe HOW to investigate a kind of question (which tools in which order); 'block' skills describe WHAT a block means (field meanings, rules, relations). Shows how many blocks of the active dump each block skill binds. Filter by kind or a query.

query.description: Optional words to rank skills by relevance.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_useSkill
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Activate one skill by name and return its full guidance (Markdown body), bound blocks, field meanings, declared rules/relations, resources and the skills it composes. Call this BEFORE answering whenever a skill's description matches the user's request.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_readSkillResource
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a resource file (checklist, enum table, struct JSON, examples) that a skill lists. Path is relative to the skill folder; capped at 8000 characters.

path.description: Relative resource path as listed by nvm_useSkill.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_searchKnowledge
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the text of ALL skills (including block skills that bind nothing in this dump) for a business term such as 'reset', 'odometer', 'DTC'. Use once before concluding that some information is not in the dump.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_checkRules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluate the declarative rules (single-block invariants) and relations (write ORDER, CO-WRITE, cross-block VALUE consistency, PRESENCE, REFERENCE) declared by skills against the active dump, and report violations with evidence. Pass skill names to check only those (a playbook also checks the skills it composes).

skills.description: Optional skill names to check (default: all).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_timeline
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show blocks in WRITE ORDER (by the generic sequence hint), with version numbers per logical block. Use 'around' to see what was written immediately before/after a block (window), 'match' to filter by name globs, 'latestOnly' for the newest instance per block, 'newestFirst' to start from the most recent writes.

around.description: Center on the newest write of this block.

latestOnly.description: Only newest instance per logical block.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_blockHistory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return every stored version of ONE logical block (same identity) in write order, with the decoded fields that changed on each write (before → after, numeric delta). Use to understand how a value evolved, when a counter incremented, or which write introduced a bad value.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_queryFields
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Tabulate decoded field values across MANY blocks (one row per block, one column per field path such as 'Counter', 'Hist[].Reason', '$sequence', '$versions'), optionally filtered with a 'where' expression. Use to compare a field across a block family or to find blocks with suspicious values.

latestOnly.description: Only newest instance per logical block (default true).

languageModelTools.name: nvm_evaluate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluate a whitelisted expression per block, or per block PAIR when 'other' is given (use self.X / other.Y). Supports field paths, $sequence/$offset/$length/$versions/$isLatest/$attr.<key>, comparisons, && || !, arithmetic, bit ops and exists()/count()/sum()/any()/all()/distinct()/min/max/abs/bit/contains. Use to verify logical or business relationships between fields and blocks.

other.description: Optional partner blocks for self/other expressions.

languageModelTools.name: nvm_correlateWrites
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Quantify the WRITE relationship between two block families: for every write of A, the nearest write of B in write order — how many A writes are accompanied by B within 'within' steps, whether B comes before or after, and A writes with no B nearby (orphans).

scripts.compile: npm run compile:core && npm run server:build
